questions.question: For the red blood cell, the muscle cell and the root hair cell, name one structural feature and the function it allows.
questions.expected_answer: Red blood cell: no nucleus, which allows more room for haemoglobin to carry oxygen (also a dented disc shape giving a large surface area). Muscle cell: many mitochondria, which release the energy needed for contraction (also long, with sliding protein fibres). Root hair cell: a long thin extension, which increases the surface area for absorbing water and minerals from the soil.

questions.question: Define tissue, organ and system, and illustrate each level with the heart.
questions.expected_answer: A tissue is a group of similar cells performing the same function, for example cardiac muscle tissue. An organ is several different tissues working together to perform a function, for example the heart, made of muscle, nervous, connective and epithelial tissue. A system is a group of organs working together, for example the circulatory system of heart and blood vessels. The order is cell, tissue, organ, system, organism.

questions.question: Explain what a stem cell is and where stem cells are found, and state whether a specialised muscle cell has different DNA from a nerve cell in the same person.
questions.expected_answer: A stem cell is an unspecialised cell that can divide repeatedly and whose daughter cells can develop into specialised cells of different types. They are found in early embryos, in adult bone marrow (making blood cells) and in umbilical cord blood. A muscle cell and a nerve cell have identical DNA, 46 chromosomes each; they differ because different genes are active in each.
